clue.text: Right moan, no good

indicators.note: no good tells us to drop G, the usual abbreviation for good, from the complaint

parts.note: to moan is to gripe

explanation.surface: Someone complains about a correct decision, calling it worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' is used in the sense of ready or fit, as when the time is right for action.
explanation.definitionFit: When conditions are fit or ready for something, people say the time is ripe, a looser synonym.

clue.text: About to go into orbit, so prepared in technological area

indicators.note: to go into means the abbreviation for about is inserted
prepared means the letters are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A craft is about to enter orbit, ready in a technical field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' gives ROBOTIS from the two words; 'About' looks like 'concerning' but is the circa abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Robotics is the field of engineering that builds robots, a technological area.

clue.text: No more sheep on island for meat

parts.note: something past is gone, no more
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: Sheep have vanished from an island, so meat is scarce.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is a spiced, smoked cured beef, a kind of meat.

clue.text: Sign of omission made by guy perhaps consuming hour on a job

parts.note: a job is a post

indicators.note: consuming means one piece swallows another, so the cord takes the hour letter inside

parts.note: a guy is a rope that steadies a tent, so it is an example of rope

explanation.surface: A mark showing letters left out is apparently made by some fellow taking an hour over his work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guy' looks like a man but is a guy rope; 'on' places the rope after A POST in this across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised comma punctuation mark shows where letters have been left out, as in don't.

clue.text: Tiresome person beginning to overdo sauce

parts.note: a pest is an annoying person

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An irritating cook starts to go too heavy on the sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesto is an Italian sauce of basil, pine nuts and cheese.

clue.text: Reviser using crib possibly defended by admirer

indicators.note: defended by means the admirer surrounds and protects the cot

parts.note: a suitor is an admirer who courts someone
a crib or cot is a kind of bed, so an example

explanation.surface: A copy editor cribbing from someone has a fan sheltering them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crib' tempts as cheating, but it is a baby's cot.
explanation.definitionFit: A subeditor checks and corrects copy before publication, so revises it.

clue.text: River with load of outstanding waterproof exercise apparatus

indicators.note: with load of says the river carries the other pieces as cargo inside it

parts.note: the Rhine is a major European river
a debt outstanding is owing
a mac, short for mackintosh, is a waterproof coat

explanation.surface: A river freighted with unpaid, rainproof gym equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing machine is a gym device simulating rowing, a piece of exercise apparatus.

clue.text: Rotten plonk, free

parts.note: to plonk something down is to put it
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: Cheap wine that is rotten, yet given away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plonk' tempts as cheap wine, but it is a verb: set down.
explanation.definitionFit: Putrid means decayed and foul, a synonym for rotten.

clue.text: Part of speech Oedipus repeated

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a speech in a Greek tragedy is said again.
explanation.definitionFit: Echoed means said again or reproduced, a verb synonym for repeated.

clue.text: Workers for instance carrying spades and proof of membership as well

indicators.note: carrying means the insects hold the other pieces within themselves

parts.note: worker bees are the classic crossword workers, so bees are an example
S is the abbreviation for spades in card games
an ID card proves who you are and that you belong

explanation.surface: Labourers bring shovels and their union cards along too.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides and as well are both adverbs meaning in addition, interchangeable synonyms.

clue.text: Dance tune, sort played in place with low prices

parts.note: a disco is a dance

indicators.note: played means the letters are performed in a new order

explanation.surface: A dance tune of some kind is played in a bargain shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A discount store is a shop selling goods cheaply, a place with low prices.

clue.text: Delight in network reversed by irritation

indicators.note: reversed tells us to read the word for a mesh or net from right to left

parts.note: a web is a network
an itch is an irritation of the skin

explanation.surface: Someone takes pleasure in an online network turned against them by annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: To bewitch someone is to charm or enchant them, so it is a verb synonym for delight.

clue.text: Beginning to move violently out of the ark

parts.note: to thresh is to thrash about, moving violently
something out of Noah's ark is very old, an idiom for antiquated

explanation.surface: An instruction to start flailing wildly once off Noah's boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginning' is a noun here, the outset, as in being on the threshold of a career.
explanation.definitionFit: A threshold is the point of entry or outset of something, so a noun synonym for beginning.

clue.text: Row one? That's in front part of vehicle

indicators.note: in places the numeral letter within the word for the vehicle's front

parts.note: the nose of a car or plane is its front
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a row of seats is the front one in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' tempts as a line of seats, but it is the rhyme-with-cow sense: a din.
explanation.definitionFit: A row in the sense of a loud racket or din is a synonym of noise.

clue.text: Funny nod put into wordless performance following firm rhythm

indicators.note: following means the company abbreviation comes first and the rest follows it

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: put into: the shuffled letters go inside the silent show

parts.note: a mime is a performance without words

indicators.note: funny means the letters of the two words are made odd and rearranged

explanation.surface: A comic nod is inserted into a silent act after a company's beat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' gives POUNDT; compound time is a musical metre, so 'rhythm' is the definition, not part of the performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Compound time is a musical metre such as six-eight, where beats divide into threes: a kind of rhythm.

clue.text: Critic elected to turn up and watch screening quietly

indicators.note: to turn up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: in means elected, as a party voted in

indicators.note: screening means the watch hides the soft letter within it

parts.note: a ticker is slang for a watch
P is the musical abbreviation piano, quietly

explanation.surface: A reviewer elected to show up and watch a quiet film showing.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitpicker finds fault over petty details, a pedantic critic.

clue.text: Booking awful act, in for walloping

parts.note: a gig is a booking for a performer

indicators.note: awful means the letters are put in a terrible jumble

explanation.surface: A dreadful act gets a gig and takes a beating.
explanation.definitionFit: Walloping as an adjective means huge, a synonym for gigantic.

clue.text: Trusting legal document to protect river over year

indicators.note: to protect means the document wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: a deed is a legal document

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the river sits above the year

parts.note: the Wye is a river on the England-Wales border

explanation.surface: A credulous person relies on a legal paper to shield a river for a year.
explanation.definitionFit: Dewy-eyed means naive and innocent, so trusting.

clue.text: Plain for all to see, rabbit with energy off and running

parts.note: U is the British film certificate for a universal audience, suitable for all to see

indicators.note: off means the energy letter is removed from the chatter word

parts.note: to rabbit on is British slang for to chatter, to natter
E is the physics symbol for energy
a machine that is running is active, working

explanation.surface: Someone talks plainly in public, rabbiting on until they run out of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' drops E from NATTER, leaving NATTR; 'Plain' tempts as flat land but describes looks.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain, said of a person's looks, means not attractive, so a synonym for unattractive.

clue.text: See supervisor in strike holding his ground

indicators.note: holding means the blow word contains the mixed letters

parts.note: a bop is a strike or blow

indicators.note: ground means the word is crushed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A manager on a picket line keeps his footing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' gives ISH. A see is a diocese, so 'See supervisor' is the cleric in charge of one.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop oversees a see, the diocese under his authority.

clue.text: Pro with excellence losing it late

parts.note: for means pro, in favour of

indicators.note: losing means the two letters of it are removed from the excellence word

parts.note: merit is excellence

explanation.surface: A professional with real quality loses it in old age.
explanation.definitionFit: Late means former, as in the late chairman, previous holder.

clue.text: Presses right ahead in middle of crisis

indicators.note: in tells us the two short pieces sit inside the central letters
middle of picks the central pair of letters from the six-letter word

parts.note: on means ahead or forward, as in go on

explanation.surface: A pressing need to act decisively during an emergency.
explanation.definitionFit: To iron clothes is to press them, so presses and irons are verb synonyms.

clue.text: Academic spirit in journal apart from opening that's fantastic

indicators.note: in puts the degree and the drink inside the shortened diary
apart from opening means the first letter of the journal word is dropped

parts.note: a diary is a journal
an MA, a Master of Arts, is an academic
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A scholarly ghost appears in a magazine, minus its first page, which is amazing.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantastic in its older sense means existing only in fantasy, so it matches made-up or unreal.

clue.text: Sailor dismissed roughly

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
in cricket a batsman dismissed is out

explanation.surface: A seaman was thrown out with little ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: About means approximately, a synonym for roughly.

clue.text: Ridicule after drone gets small rise

indicators.note: after means the word for ridicule comes behind the other piece

parts.note: a drone is a low hum
to mock is to ridicule

explanation.surface: Scorn follows a buzzing noise and earns a small laugh.
explanation.definitionFit: A hummock is a low mound or hillock, a small rise in the ground.

clue.text: Obviously nothing jolly about lieutenant in retreat

parts.note: O is the round figure zero, nothing

indicators.note: about means the word for very goes round the reversed officer

parts.note: jolly is British slang for very, as in jolly good

indicators.note: in retreat means the officer's abbreviation goes backwards

explanation.surface: Plainly there is nothing cheerful about an officer falling back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retreat' gives TL; 'jolly' is British slang for very, not cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtly means openly or plainly, a synonym for obviously.

clue.text: Be responsible for a particular class

parts.note: a means per, as in twice a day, twice per day
pet as an adjective means particular or favourite, as in pet subject
rate means class or grade, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: Take charge of one specific category.
explanation.definitionFit: To perpetrate a crime or blunder is to commit it, being the one responsible.

clue.text: Race ending in fracas? Matter for rumination

indicators.note: ending in picks the last letter of the brawl word

parts.note: cud is food chewed again by ruminant animals such as cows

explanation.surface: A race ends in a brawl, which gives people something to chew over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rumination' looks like thinking, but it is the cow's literal chewing.
explanation.definitionFit: To scud is to race along swiftly, as clouds do before the wind.
